statement: For a finite group action, the size of the group equals the size of an orbit times the size of the stabilizer of any point in that orbit.
conditions: A finite group G acts on a set S
s is in S
conclusion: |G|=|Orbit(s)|*|Stab(s)|.

Prove divisibility facts for group actions.

conclusion: |G| is the sum of sizes of conjugacy classes; |C_G(x)|*[conjugacy_class_size_of_x]=|G|.

Prove results about p-groups and simple groups.
common_misuses: Confusing centralizer with center.
Assuming all conjugacy classes have the same size.

source: Artin Algebra, Second Edition; rewritten seed rule
name: Smith normal form divisibility correction
statement: After clearing the first row and column, if the pivot does not divide some remaining entry, add that column to the pivot column and use Euclidean reduction again to produce a smaller pivot.
conditions: The pivot row and column are cleared
Some remaining entry is not divisible by the pivot
conclusion: The matrix must be further reduced before the pivot can be accepted as an invariant factor.
typical_uses: Catch premature diagonal forms that fail d_i | d_{i+1}.
Finish Smith normal form computations correctly.
common_misuses: Stopping at a diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries do not divide successively.
Changing entries by non-unimodular operations.

source: Artin Algebra, Second Edition; rewritten seed rule
name: Real quadratic integer rings have infinitely many units
statement: The group of units in the ring of integers of a real quadratic number field is infinite.
conditions: R is the ring of integers in a real quadratic number field
conclusion: R^* is infinite.
typical_uses: Explain why real quadratic unit groups differ from imaginary quadratic unit groups.
Support Pell-type arguments.
common_misuses: Assuming only +/-1 are units in every quadratic integer ring.
Confusing real and imaginary quadratic fields.

source: Artin Algebra, Second Edition; rewritten seed rule
name: Unit norm criterion in real quadratic fields
statement: For a real quadratic integer alpha, being a unit is detected by norm: alpha is a unit when its norm is plus or minus 1.
conditions: alpha is an algebraic integer in a real quadratic field
conclusion: N(alpha)=+/-1 implies alpha is a unit; units lie on norm hyperbolas in the two real embeddings.
typical_uses: Find units in rings such as Z[sqrt(2)].
Translate unit questions into Pell-type norm equations.
common_misuses: Using absolute value of one embedding instead of field norm.
Forgetting the conjugate embedding.

source: Artin Algebra, Second Edition; rewritten seed rule
name: Quartic discriminant and resolvent decision table
statement: For an irreducible quartic, combine the square class of the discriminant with reducibility of the resolvent cubic: square discriminant and irreducible resolvent gives A4; nonsquare discriminant and irreducible resolvent gives S4; split resolvent gives D2; one-root resolvent with nonsquare discriminant gives D4 or C4.
conditions: f is an irreducible quartic
D is its discriminant
g is its resolvent cubic
conclusion: The pair (D square?, factorization of g) narrows the quartic Galois group as stated.
typical_uses: Diagnose quartic Galois group computations.
Avoid using discriminant alone for quartics.
common_misuses: Claiming D4 versus C4 without additional information.
Using the table when f is reducible or has repeated roots.

source: Artin Algebra, Second Edition; rewritten seed rule
name: Irreducible quintic with exactly three real roots has S5 Galois group
statement: An irreducible quintic over Q with exactly three real roots has Galois group S5, hence its roots are not solvable by radicals.
conditions: f is irreducible of degree 5 over Q
f has exactly three real roots
conclusion: Gal(f/Q)=S5 and the roots are not solvable by radicals.
typical_uses: Prove concrete quintics are not solvable by radicals from root counts.
Find a transposition from complex conjugation and a 5-cycle from transitivity.
common_misuses: Applying to reducible quintics.
Using the root-count test without proving irreducibility.
